evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese Character Database), CUHK
evidence.text: The database reports four oracle-bone examples for 還, analyzing the oracle-bone forms as 行/目/方, while bronze, seal, and manuscript forms use 辵 with 睘 as phonetic. It cites an oracle-bone example in 合集6349, 工方還, glossed as ‘the people of 工方 returned,’ and bronze examples using 還 for return and for ‘go around.’ The database itself notes a Zhouyuan oracle-bone form analyzed with 彳 and 睘, showing variation in the early analyses/forms. This is a source’s paleographic account; the glyph images were not independently inspected here.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 還

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese Character Database), CUHK
evidence.text: For later bronze and seal forms, the database identifies 辵 as the walking/semantic component and 睘 as a sound component, also proposing that 睘’s ‘round jade disc’ sense contributes to the return meaning. The second semantic contribution is the database’s interpretation; the received 說文解字 analysis only explicitly calls 睘 a sound element. The graph’s oracle-bone analysis is different, so do not project the 辵/睘 breakdown onto every earliest form.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 還

evidence.source: 說文解字, online transcription with 段玉裁 commentary
evidence.text: The received entry says ‘復也。从辵瞏聲。戶關切’ (‘return/repeat; from 辵, with 瞏 as phonetic’). Duan Yucai’s Qing commentary cites 爾雅’s ‘還，復返也’ and remarks that classical texts used 還 for the circling sense now commonly written 環. This is a historical lexicographic account, not independent proof of a component’s ancient sound or the earliest graph shape.
evidence.title: 說文解字「還」

evidence.text: The entry separates huán ‘return’ from hái adverbial uses including ‘still/remains,’ ‘more,’ ‘again,’ and ‘also.’ Under huán it gives early/classical citations: 詩經《小雅·何人斯》‘還而不入’ for returning; 《漢書·項籍傳》 for turning/look back; 《禮記·內則》 and other texts for circling; later cited uses cover restoration, repayment, and retaliation. It also records hái-type uses in Tang citations, including 柳宗元 ‘世世還復然’ for ‘still/again,’ and later examples for ‘also’ and ‘more.’ These lexicographic citations establish that the senses are attested in the cited works, but their exact composition dates and whether each sense developed directly from ‘return’ are not established by this entry alone.
evidence.kind: historical dictionary with cited textual examples
evidence.title: 還 huán、hái — 汉典

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese Character Database), CUHK
evidence.text: The database reports bronze inscription use for ‘return’ and ‘go around,’ cites 《詩經·小雅·何人斯》 for return, and distinguishes later manuscript loans: Warring States Chu slips use 還 for 懷 in 《郭店簡·尊德義》, while Mawangdui silk manuscripts use 還 for 環 ‘encircle’ and in another passage write 環 for 還 ‘return.’ These are whole-graph phonetic loan uses in those texts, separate from 睘’s role as a sound element inside the later 還 compound. The source’s claim that some manuscript spellings borrow one whole graph for another does not make the component roles the same phenomenon.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 還

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese Character Database), CUHK
evidence.text: The database quotes the bronze inscription 呂行壺, ‘伯懋父北征，唯還,’ interpreted as the return of the expedition; 散氏盤 has a use it interprets as ‘go around.’ It also cites 《詩經·小雅·何人斯》 for return, and 《荀子·王霸》 ‘禹舜還至，王業還起’ for ‘immediately.’ The bronze examples are identified by artifact name but the inspected text gives no absolute artifact dates; no date should be assigned from this source page alone.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 還

evidence.source: 教育部《異體字字典》 (Taiwan Ministry of Education)
evidence.text: The dictionary classifies 还 as a variant of 還, citing 《宋元以來俗字譜》 examples from several works and the statements 《俗書刊誤》 ‘還、俗作还’ and 《字學三正》 ‘還，俗作还.’ Its editorial explanation says the form aligns with a known scribal simplification pattern. Thus the graph 还 has a documented history as a graphic variant of 還; it is not evidence that 不 was the historical phonetic in 還. The source does not date the cited examples individually on this page.
evidence.title: [A04191-002] 还 (還) — 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: 教育部《異體字字典》 (Taiwan Ministry of Education)
evidence.text: The dictionary separately lists 还 under 不 as an appendix character, citing 《龍龕手鏡》 and 《龍龕手鑑》 with the note ‘俗不、浮二音’ and marking its status ‘待考’ (to be examined). This documents historical dictionary confusion/attestation of a graph 还 associated with 不/other readings, but does not establish that the modern simplified 還 was formed from 不 as a sound component. The dossier’s inferred 不 phonetic account is unsupported for the modern simplified form as a distinct etymological analysis.
evidence.title: [A00010-024] 还 (不) — 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: CNS11643 全字庫 (Taiwan Character Code Repository)
evidence.text: The repository gives 还 as IDS ⿺辶不 and lists pronunciations including bù and hái/huán among the readings attached to this encoded form. This is structural/code-table metadata, not historical evidence that 不 functioned as a phonetic component in the simplification or in 還’s older forms.
evidence.title: 字形資訊 — 还 — 全字庫 CNS11643

evidence.text: For 還, the source lists modern Mandarin huán and hái, Cantonese readings syun4/waan4, Tang-period *huan, and the two Guangyun fanqie entries 戶關切 (匣母, 合口二等刪韻) and 似宣切 (邪母, 合口三等仙韻), corresponding to different reading/sense groupings in its presentation. The external sources inspected do not give a directly comparable historical reconstruction for 睘 itself; therefore phonetic fit between component and compound is not independently demonstrated here. No reconstruction for an ancient name of an object depicted in 睘 is needed for this component analysis, and no such object-name claim is made.
evidence.title: 還 huán、hái — 汉典

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese Character Database), CUHK
evidence.text: The source groups ‘return,’ ‘give back,’ ‘restore,’ ‘retreat,’ and ‘encircle/rotate’ under 還, then records adverbial ‘immediately,’ ‘still,’ and choice ‘or/still’ uses. This supports the existence of varied traditional uses, not a proven linear chronology among them. The received Shuowen gloss ‘復’ and the cited 《詩經》 text support ‘return’ as an early documented sense; the exact semantic bridges to ‘still,’ ‘also,’ ‘more,’ and ‘immediately’ remain underexplained in the inspected sources. Do not derive those modern senses merely from their order in a dictionary list.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 還

evidence.text: The entry distinguishes the oracle-bone analysis (行/目/方, with a separate Zhouyuan 彳/睘 form) from later bronze and seal forms analyzed as 辵 with 睘. It also gives the cited bronze example 呂行壺 and the oracle-bone example 合集6349, 工方還. The page supplies form descriptions, but its linked glyph files could not be fetched here, so these are source descriptions rather than direct image inspection.

evidence.text: The received entry reads 還, glosses it 復也, and analyzes it 从辵瞏聲; the page also gives 戶關切 and Duan Yucai’s commentary. The source page is a transcription with an accompanying seal-form image link, but I did not inspect the image pixels.

This is a modern digital drawing/redrawing of a historical script form, not a photograph of an ancient artifact. The Commons file page itself failed to open in the tool, so the listed provenance and rights were visible only in search-result content and are not selected as a glyph asset.

gaps: No glyph image was visually inspected; the paleographic forms and interpretations are reported from database descriptions only.

The earliest oracle-bone reading has competing/variant structural analyses: CUHK describes 行/目/方 forms, and a Zhouyuan 彳/睘 form; the transition from this analysis to the later 辵/睘 graph is not fully demonstrated in the inspected sources.
The oracle-bone corpus example is identified as 合集6349, but the opened entry does not provide an absolute inscription date or independent artifact context.

The inspected sources do not supply a verified historical reconstruction for 睘 alongside a reconstruction for 還 in the same reconstruction system. The phonetic role is supported by Shuowen’s explicit assertion and later componental convention, but sound correspondence was not independently checked.
The lexical path from ‘return’ to hái ‘still/yet/also/more’ is not established by a dated chain of contextual attestations. Dictionary gloss grouping cannot supply that chronology.

The early date and precise manuscript evidence for the simplified variant 还 are not individually established on the MOE page; it cites a corpus of Song-Yuan onward popular forms and older variant dictionaries without item-by-item dates.

The older independent dictionary graph 还 listed under 不 has readings and status marked uncertain by MOE; its connection, if any, to the later 還 variant is not established. It should not be used to claim 不 was 還’s phonetic component.

No image candidate is selected: although the Commons search result described a possible redrawn seal-style vector and reuse terms, the actual Commons source page and direct image file could not be opened to verify provenance and rights. CUHK’s linked historical glyph image files also failed to fetch, and Xiaoxuetang was inaccessible.

The source descriptions support a distinction between oracle-bone forms and later 辵/睘 forms, but the actual glyph pixels were not visually inspected. Dates and artifact-level provenance for a specific image candidate therefore remain unverified.
